correctness.rationale: The tight-frame Gram identity gives exactly the zero-sum coordinate model. Dividing by the least nonzero absolute projection converts max-min to the complete sign-group norm minimization. For each sign count \(p+q=d+1\), Cauchy and group-size constraints give \(\sum_i b_i^2\ge(d+1)\max(p,q)/\min(p,q)\); equality forces constant magnitude within each sign group. Explicit zero-sum witnesses are reconstructed by the frame map and have unit norm. Balanced cardinalities yield exact squared thresholds \(1/d\) (odd dimensions) and \(1/(d+2)\) (even dimensions). Equality sign classes and antipodal counts are exhaustive, while homogeneity proves ball coverage and failure below threshold. Standard-library exact rational tests for \(2\le d\le50\) and finite random samples supplement but do not replace the proof.

evidence: Akopyan–Polyanskii (arXiv:2609.36163v1) announce the general relative plank sum theorem; for \(d+1\) equal central unit-ball planks it implies only \(t\ge1/(d+1)\), versus the proved asymptotic scale \(d^{-1/2}\). Their full text was inaccessible.

Jiang–Polyanskii, arXiv:1703.10550v2, Theorem 1: total spherical zone width is at least \(\pi\), so for \(d+1\) equal zones the necessary condition is \(t\ge\sin(\pi/(2(d+1)))\). This is attained by the regular triangular normal arrangement when \(d=2\), but is strictly weaker than the constructed threshold for \(d\ge3\).
Verreault, DOI:10.1112/blms.70230, Sections 3 and 4.2, materially inspected as open full text, gives general Ball and Fejes Toth facts, not a fixed regular-simplex-normal width formula.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The global inequalities cover the planar sharp threshold and give necessary bounds in higher dimensions, but fail to imply the construction, optimality or uniqueness of the two-level profiles in even \(d\ge4\). The odd-dimensional construction is prior-covered by the separate 2024 equimodular simplex argument; only the even-dimensional extension is treated as new. The full 2026 motivating manuscript was inaccessible, a residual risk.

originality.rationale: The significant unreported component is the exact fixed regular-simplex-normal threshold and all unequal-level extremizers in every even dimension \(d\ge4\). The 2017 zone theorem already gives the sharp \(d=2\) threshold. The 2024 simplex min-max discussion exhibits the balanced equimodular construction in odd dimensions, and the tight-frame identity then supplies the same odd-dimensional value; those special cases are explicitly acknowledged as prior-covered. General Ball/Fejes Toth theorems do not give the higher even-dimensional threshold or all equality lines. Beyond known planar and odd-dimensional benchmarks, the theorem classifies every higher even dimension \(d\ge4\), where the extremizer must have unequal sign-group magnitudes \((d+2)/d\); it also determines the exact spherical width and binomial count of worst directions. This infinite-family parity contrast is structural, not an arbitrary isolated number or table recomputation.
